summary: Today’s pulse tracks Zelenskyy signals surprise at Trump claim of Russia-Ukraine ‘energy ceasefire’ but would back it if Moscow does – live updates, Poland detains man suspected of planning assassination of PM Tusk, and Abdul El-Sayed: Democrats must ‘win by massive numbers’ to fend off Trump election denial. Across Guardian and BBC, the strongest repeated signals are ukraine, ceasefire, and trump. In the background, Trump announces partial ceasefire in Ukraine war as Zelenskyy says deal is ‘news to me’ and Middle East crisis live: Riyadh airport hit again as Houthis claim attacks, including strike that killed 12 keep the wider picture in motion.

headlines.title: Zelenskyy signals surprise at Trump claim of Russia-Ukraine ‘energy ceasefire’ but would back it if Moscow does – live updates
headlines.description: Ukraine’s president reportedly says Kyiv would accept a deal if Moscow does after US president posts announcement with no detail on social media Trump announces partial ceasefire in Ukraine war as Zelenskyy says deal is ‘news to me’ In a telephone call with the Ukrainian leader, von der Leyen posted on X that she “fully supported the call of President Zelenskyy for a ceasefire that would protect global food supplies and energy infrastructure in Ukraine and Russia. “Ukraine supports the ceasefire, and it’s important for Russia to support it as well. We are awaiting details from the American side. From our Ukrainian side, there is always FULL support for de-escalation steps, protection of lives, and the necessary decisions to end the war and ensure lasting peace.”

headlines.title: Poland detains man suspected of planning assassination of PM Tusk
headlines.description: Police received credible information about possible attacks against Donald Tusk and his defence minister.

headlines.title: Abdul El-Sayed: Democrats must ‘win by massive numbers’ to fend off Trump election denial
headlines.description: Democratic Senate candidate’s remarks come as Trump has long baselessly claimed his 2020 election loss was stolen Democrats must “win by massive numbers” during November’s federal midterm elections because Donald Trump and his Republican allies are bound to try to sow doubt about the integrity of the results, Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed of Michigan said on Sunday. El-Sayed’s comments on NBC’s Meet the Press came with the Democrats favored to win control of the House of Representatives during the 3 November midterms – and polls show that the party could also win Senate seats in states that traditionally elect Republicans and gain a majority there, too.

headlines.title: Trump announces partial ceasefire in Ukraine war as Zelenskyy says deal is ‘news to me’
headlines.description: Ukrainian president earlier rejected US call for Kyiv to stop bombing oil refineries, saying Moscow must first end attacks on energy infrastructure US politics – live updates Donald Trump has announced an energy ceasefire between Ukraine and Russia, apparently without consulting Volodymyr Zelenskyy, who said the deal to stop long-range attacks was “news to me”. In a social media post, the US president claimed the two sides had reached an agreement. “Effective immediately, there is an ENERGY CEASEFIRE in the War between Russia and Ukraine. Both parties have agreed. Do not break it!” he wrote on Truth Social.

headlines.title: Middle East crisis live: Riyadh airport hit again as Houthis claim attacks, including strike that killed 12
headlines.description: Houthi military spokesman says Iran-backed group carried out several targeted attacks Some more Gulf reaction to Houthi’s deadly airport attack and continued threats to target Saudi airspace. In a significant message, the United Arab Emirates has issued a statement in solidarity with Saudi Arabia – expressing support for “all measures aimed at safeguarding the kingdom’s security and stability”. The UAE message is improtant given the major rupture in relations this year between the two oil-rich kingdoms, first sparked by lingering divisions in Yemen, and made worse by the Iran War and arguments over oil prices which led to the UAE quitting OPEC (currently led by the Saudis) after six decades of membership. Saturday’s incident comes amid an escalation of missile strikes by Yemen’s Iran-aligned Houthis ⁠on the kingdom. The airport has already been attacked twice this ​week, leaving four people dead and ‌others wounded, and ‌badly damaging an aircraft. The Houthis have repeatedly attacked Saudi airports, oil facilities and tankers after a truce in their long-running war with Yemen’s Riyadh-backed government unravelled in July.

headlines.title: Volkswagen boss backs EU plan to bolster domestic European industry
headlines.description: Oliver Blume says ‘Made in Europe’ rules to counter rapid rise of lower-price Chinese brands ‘must reward real value creation’ The boss of Volkswagen has backed EU proposals to boost its domestic industry, arguing European carmakers need to be able to “compete under comparable conditions” with Chinese rivals. Oliver Blume said “Made in Europe” rules from the EU “must reward real value creation in Europe”, speaking in Paris before the motor show this week.

headlinePool.title: Riyadh airport hit again after deadly Houthi missile attack, Saudi authorities say
headlinePool.description: Unidentified projectile strikes King Khalid airport as escalating attacks threaten to draw more countries into Yemen conflict Middle East crisis live – latest updates Analysis: attack will force rethink of Trump strategy A projectile hit a passenger terminal at the airport in Riyadh on Sunday, the day after a deadly missile attack on the facility carried out by Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthi rebel group killed 13 people. An unidentified projectile hit terminal 4 at King Khalid international airport, starting a fire and causing injuries, according to Saudi authorities. Air defences also intercepted a cruise missile in the vicinity of the airport. It was the latest of several attacks on the airport in the past week.

headlinePool.title: Saudi Arabia's Riyadh airport hit by second Houthi strike in two days
headlinePool.description: The Yemeni group says it carried out attacks that killed 13 people over the weekend and targeted two airports and oil facilities.

headlinePool.title: Donald Tusk says man accused of plotting to kill him detained
headlinePool.description: Polish PM praises police for ‘swift and decisive action’ after threat against him and defence minister revealed The Polish prime minister, Donald Tusk, said on Sunday that a man accused of plotting to assassinate him and his defence minister had been detained. “The man threatening an attack has been detained,” Tusk wrote on X, praising the police for their “swift and decisive action”.

headlinePool.title: Trump’s deal with Putin will have little impact on US diesel prices, experts say
headlinePool.description: Analysts say fuel will take weeks to ship and quantity is too small to affect prices, while full deal is unlikely to be met given damage to Russian refineries Trump announces partial ceasefire but Zelenskyy says deal is ‘news to me’ Donald Trump’s deal with Vladimir Putin to temporarily lift sanctions on US imports of Russian diesel will have little “meaningful” effect on motorists and businesses in the US and overseas, energy and foreign policy analysts have predicted. The US president infuriated Volodymyr Zelenskyy when he announced the deal on Friday, writing on Truth Social that the agreement with his Russia counterpart to supply millions of tonnes of diesel was essential to reduce fuel prices in the US, which have soared after his decision to go to war against Iran.

headlinePool.title: Andy Burnham says it is clear Russia interfered in Brexit referendum
headlinePool.description: PM says he asked question upon entering No 10 but does not reveal who gave him ‘clear answer’ that Russia meddled Andy Burnham has said it is clear Russia interfered in the Brexit referendum, after seeking answers on the Kremlin’s involvement in the 2016 vote when he entered Downing Street. Burnham said he had asked whether Moscow had attempted to influence the referendum and received a confirmation that it had.

headlinePool.title: Riyadh airport attacks another dangerous moment in already tense conflict
headlinePool.description: While the physical damage from Houthi attacks can be quickly repaired, the Saudi reputation for stability is taking a battering.

headlinePool.title: Children among 139 dead after boat capsizes off Djibouti, UN says
headlinePool.description: The boat was travelling from Djibouti to Yemen with 305 people on board, when it capsized near the port town of Obock on Thursday night.

headlinePool.title: Poland stabbings driven by online glorification of violence, Tusk says
headlinePool.description: The PM was speaking after violent attacks at Polish schools this week left one dead and others injured.

headlinePool.title: Zack Polanski signals Green party overhaul after row over Zionism vote
headlinePool.description: Rapid growth means structures need to change and give leaders greater control, Polanski says in Guardian article Zack Polanski: How we’re transforming British politics Zack Polanski has signalled a potential overhaul of the Green party’s cherished grassroots democracy, calling for leaders to have greater control over strategic direction after a divisive vote equating Zionism with racism. The Green party leader has also questioned whether political parties should seek to define what members believe, in his strongest criticism yet of a motion that has provoked bitter divisions, international condemnation and calls for his resignation.
